newsitem.title: BENIN: IMF agrees $40 million loan for Benin.
newsitem.headline: IMF agrees $40 million loan for Benin.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has approved a $40 million three-year loan to Benin under the West African country's Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility, Finance Minister Moise Mensah said.
The credit aims to support the government's economic reform programme and the first annual loan of $13 million will be disbursed in two equal instalments, the first of which is available immediately.

Benin's last ESAF expired in March 1996. The IMF said the economic programme for 1996-99 aimed at annual real gross domestic product growth of over five percent, annual inflation of about three percent, and a reduction in the external current account deficit, excluding grants, to about 5.5 percent of GDP by 1999.

Benin is targeting GDP growth of 5.5 percent for 1996 and 5.8 percent for 1997. The external current account deficit is put at 7.3 percent of GDP for 1996 and 6.4 percent in 1997, from 8.6 percent in 1995.

The government aims to reduce the overall budget deficit, excluding grants, to 6.6 percent of GDP in 1996 and 6.2 percent in 1997, from seven percent in 1995. Measures to increase revenue will include a reduction of customs exemptions, and tax increases on certain products.
Mensah said the privatisation programme would continue, concentrating on state-run hotels and vegetable oil processor Societe Nationale pour l'Industrie des Corps Gras (SONICOG).
An action plan for developing production of cotton, Benin's main export, is due to be adopted by the end of 1996.
Talks with the Paris Club of official creditors on a reduction of Benin's $1.4 billion debt are scheduled for September 23.
